previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with hypotension during an outpatient blood transfusion, following a drop in hematocrit to 19.7% and an INR of 2.6. He had a history of recurrent GI bleeding on anticoagulation for a mechanical aortic valve. Warfarin was held, and he received multiple transfusions totaling 7 units of PRBCs. An upper endoscopy revealed gastric angioectasias in a watermelon stomach pattern, which were successfully treated with argon-plasma coagulation. Heparin was bridged post-procedure and discontinued when INR reached 1.6, with warfarin restarted at 3 mg nightly and target INR lowered to 2.0–2.5. Heart failure was managed with cautious diuresis using torsemide after bleeding control. He developed delirium, likely exacerbated by oxycodone for left shoulder calcific tendinitis, confirmed by X-ray and treated with a steroid injection. Mental status improved with medication taper. He was discharged home with services, stable hemoglobin, and plans for close outpatient monitoring of INR and volume status.

INDICATION:  Patient with CHF exacerbation, admitted for intravenous diuresis,
please assess pleural effusion or vascular congestion.

COMPARISON:  ___ and multiple chest radiographs spanning from
___ to ___.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral chest x-ray.

FINDINGS:  There is blunting of both costophrenic angles with right basilar
discoid atelectasis seen in the frontal view and confirmed in the lateral
view.  Vascular cephalization and mild pulmonary edema are present as well. 
Moderate-to-severe cardiomegaly is stable compared with prior radiograph. 
Sternotomy wires are intact.  Pacemaker with leads in standard position is
seen.

IMPRESSION:  Cardiac decompensation with pulmonary vascular congestion,
interstitial edema and bilateral pleural effusion.
